description: PRISMA (PRecursore IperSpettrale della Missione Applicativa) is the hyperspectral Earth observation satellite owned by the Italian Space Agency (ASI), launched on 22 March 2019 on a VEGA launcher and operating from an orbit at 615 km. Its imaging spectrometer records the visible and near infrared and short-wave infrared spectrum at 30 m spatial resolution, alongside a panchromatic camera at 5 m. The satellite was built by a grouping led by OHB Italia, with the hyperspectral instrument from Leonardo; mission control is at Fucino and data processing at the Matera Space Center. Coverage is global on request, as scenes are tasked and archived; resolution is 30 m hyperspectral and 5 m panchromatic. Format and access: products are ordered through the PRISMA mission portal at prisma.asi.it, which requires an ASI user account. Licence: not stated on the pages read; product terms sit behind the login. Cost could not be read. Caveats: on 28 September 2026 the portal said 'Registration is temporarily disabled', so new users cannot get access, and scene availability depends on past tasking. Simulation uses: spectral mapping of land cover, surface materials, vegetation stress and water quality around infrastructure, useful for hazard exposure and environmental condition inputs. Related records: the MYSA remote sensing open data catalogue is another national space agency archive in the catalogue.
